reason: The static gate sequence for Eventar is repeated every phase and its failure modes are recurring: stale generated type folders after next build, and heavy gates colliding. Nothing in the library covers it, so it gets a project skill.

The baseline is stale after K3. Two gate facts were learned the hard way: a load-induced test failure, and an em-dash copy breach caught only by self-review. Both are pre-commit checks that belong with the gate list.

Episode hit three vitest 5s timeouts in unrelated account/profile/invite files under peer load; they passed 78/78 when rerun alone. The skill covers the flake class but not the timeout signature or the isolated-rerun step.

Episode hit a 6-minute incremental tsc stall and a 2 GB OOM, traced to a gitignored stale tsbuildinfo and to supabase-js's inferred select row type. Both are non-obvious and the gate skill is where a future session will look first.

Full vitest run needs local-stack Supabase URL and keys. With no env, 46 DB-gated files fail at import with "supabaseUrl is required". Passing the local values as process env, plus an empty temp .env.local (tests/helpers/env.ts throws if the file is missing), gave 187 files passed and 46 skipped. The gate is green on the local stack, not on Seoul.

The em-dash scan flagged lines that were reshaped, not newly written: a header that already said "Times in HKT — <clock>" was rewritten with a variable zone and so matched the + filter. Scan results need a check of whether the copy is new or moved.

The recorded baseline is stale (2026-10-14). The 2026-10-16 run gave vitest 1501 passed and 404 skipped, eslint 12 problems (1 error, 11 warnings, all pre-existing), and next build 39 routes. The next session needs these numbers to read its delta.

Landing a commit range onto main was gated only in the dirty worktree. Gating the exact tip in a clean detached worktree caught nothing new here but is the check that proves what gets pushed. The recorded vitest baseline is stale for main after 9cb0de2.

The agent reported two extra gates as failing before its edits, without a saved baseline to measure "unchanged" against. It also saw a flake and had to decide how to report it. The static-gates skill should record both the baseline step and the flake rule.

Gate-failure triage here lists flakes and load, but not the clock. A suite that goes red after a set hour is a deterministic clock assertion, not a flake, and rerunning it hides the cause. This episode lost time to exactly that.

The tip gate was run in the background with a sentinel and polled; the sentinel-plus-section read is a reusable way to run the four gates without blocking, and nothing in the skill yet says how to wait on them.
The skill names a path that no longer exists; the failing file in the 2026-10-23 run is under app/events/[id]/edit/. The flake recurred and the rerun evidence should be recorded.

The baseline line for check:ui-colours and check:ui-primitives is from 2026-10-22. On 2026-10-24 both failed again. The HEAD comparison showed the same violations already present, but at shifted line numbers, so the skill should say to compare by line text and to prove pre-existence against HEAD.

The 2026-10-24 tip gate failed in two more component tests with the same flake pattern. Adding them to the known-flake record keeps the next session from misreading them as regressions, while still requiring the isolated rerun.

The recorded vitest baseline predates the RLS-inclusive run, so a later session cannot tell whether a new count is a regression or a different suite. The 2026-10-25 tip-gate result gives the current reference.
